subject.title: [Bug]: Discord routing / mention-gating issue in OpenClaw

question: Should Discord preflight adopt strict active-target scoping that suppresses the current/default agent when another configured agent, role target, or quoted/later mention signal means the current agent is not being addressed?
rationale: The source gap is concrete, but the requested behavior changes stable Discord routing precedence, role semantics, and bot-loop behavior for existing multi-agent guild setups.

options.title: Adopt Strict Active-Target Scoping
options.body: Implement Discord-owned target resolution before default routing, drop messages that target other configured agents, scope mention text to the opening attention window, and require live Discord proof.

options.title: Split Into Narrower Trackers
options.body: Keep this broader issue as coordination while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/13487, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/7717, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80235 own separate slices.

options.title: Document Current Default-Owner Behavior
options.body: Treat current default routing plus ignoreOtherMentions and allowBots policy as the intended contract and close or narrow requests that conflict with that behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt Strict Active-Target Scoping
recommendation.body: Implement Discord-owned target resolution before default routing, drop messages that target other configured agents, scope mention text to the opening attention window, and require live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has both the prior decision-context comments and the strongest code-history signal for Discord mention/routing policy.
